module.title: Unit 12: Travellers' Tales: Travel, Transport & Relative Clauses
module.objective: Narrate travel adventures, transport choices, and provide additional details about people and places using defining relative clauses.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Travellers' Tales and Amazing Transport
subModules.grammarFocus: Present Perfect Simple and Relative Clauses

content.summary: Welcome to Unit 12. In this reading module, you will explore stories about travellers, different kinds of transport, and exciting places around the world. You will learn how to read for specific details and understand how to talk about life experiences using grammar patterns.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Present Perfect Simple for life experiences and defining relative clauses with who, which, and where.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words related to travel, transport, and accommodation.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning texts to find specific names, dates, and transport types.

learningObjectives: Understand the main ideas of short A2 reading passages about travel.
Locate specific details regarding transport methods and destinations.
Recognize grammar structures like the Present Perfect Simple and relative clauses in texts.

contextWarmup.prompt: When you go on holiday, what is your favorite way to travel long distances?
options: Taking a fast train or tram
contextWarmup.explanation: Trains and trams are popular transport choices for viewing scenery during short and long trips.

rules: Use the Present Perfect Simple (have/has + past participle) to talk about life experiences when the exact time is not important.
Use 'who' for people, 'which' for things, and 'where' for places in relative clauses.
Use the Past Simple when you mention a specific time in the past, such as yesterday or last year.

commonTrap.trapTitle: Confusing Past Simple and Present Perfect
commonTrap.explanation: Learners often use the Present Perfect when they mention a specific past time.
commonTrap.wrong: I have visited Bali last year.
commonTrap.correct: I visited Bali last year. Use Past Simple with specific past times.

grammarFormulas.description: Build correct sentences for affirmative experiences:

items.collocation: ride a motorbike / buy a motorbike

items.exampleSentence: I had to catch the train but I missed the bus.
items.collocation: catch a train / catch a bus

items.exampleSentence: My uncle is someone I admire because he helps other people.
We arrived at the airport two hours before our flight.
items.collocation: international airport / go to the airport

content.passageTitle: Amazing Travel Adventures Around the World
paragraphs: Leo is an adventurous traveller who loves exploring new countries. He has visited over twenty nations in the last five years. Last summer, he went on a long trip across Europe. He rode a motorbike through mountain roads and took a tram in busy cities. Leo always finds comfortable accommodation in small local houses where he meets friendly residents.

Travelling by public transport is one of Leo's favorite things. He often needs to catch an early morning train or a local minibus to reach remote villages. During his trips, he meets many interesting people whom he deeply admires. Leo believes that seeing the world opens your mind and teaches you important lessons about different cultures and daily life.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Travel Stories and Relative Clauses

content.summary: Practical guide on writing about travel experiences, transport methods, and connecting sentences using relative clauses in English.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Present Perfect for Life Experiences
blueprintItems.example: I have visited three different countries in Europe.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Describing Transport and Travel
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + verb (took / travelled by) + transport method
blueprintItems.example: We travelled by train from London to Paris.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Connecting Ideas with Relative Clauses
blueprintItems.formula: Noun + relative pronoun (who / which / where) + clause
blueprintItems.example: This is the hotel where we stayed last summer.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always capitalize proper names of countries, cities, and nationalities.
mechanicsRules.badExample: i went to paris and spent time in france.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I went to Paris and spent time in France.
mechanicsRules.why: Countries, cities, and the pronoun 'I' must always start with a capital letter.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use correct past participle forms for irregular verbs in the Present Perfect.
mechanicsRules.badExample: She has went to Tokyo by plane.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: She has gone to Tokyo by plane.
mechanicsRules.why: The past participle of 'go' is 'gone' or 'been', not 'went'.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use relative pronouns correctly for people, things, and places.
mechanicsRules.badExample: He is the guide which showed us the city.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: He is the guide who showed us the city.
mechanicsRules.why: Use 'who' for people, 'which' for things, and 'where' for places.

sampleSentences.en: I have never flown in a helicopter before.
sampleSentences.id: Saya belum pernah naik helikopter sebelumnya.

sampleSentences.en: She visited Rome last year with her family.
sampleSentences.id: Dia mengunjungi Roma tahun lalu bersama keluarganya.
sampleSentences.focus: Past Simple for specific past time

sampleSentences.en: He is the guide who showed us around the old castle.
sampleSentences.id: Dia adalah pemandu yang menunjukkan kepada kami kastil tua tersebut.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: i have went to japan twice by plane
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: I have been to Japan twice by plane.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Saya telah pergi ke Jepang dua kali dengan pesawat.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Use 'been' with 'have' for travel experiences and capitalize the pronoun 'I' and country 'Japan'.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: they catched the bus to london yesterday morning
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: They caught the bus to London yesterday morning.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Mereka naik bus ke London kemarin pagi.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: The past tense of 'catch' is 'caught', and proper nouns like 'London' must be capitalized.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: she has never saw a big ship like that one
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: She has never seen a big ship like that one.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Dia belum pernah melihat kapal besar seperti itu.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: The past participle of 'see' is 'seen' after 'has never'.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: My Dream Trip
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three sentences about a memorable trip you took or want to take. Mention the transport you used, a place you visited, and what you saw.
guidedLabChallenges.example: I travelled to Bali by plane last year. I visited an amazing temple near the beach. I saw many beautiful green rice fields.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Amazing Places
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write three sentences describing a place using relative clauses (who, which, where). Mention a person who helped you, a place you went, or a thing you bought.
guidedLabChallenges.example: This is the shop where I bought my new camera. It is a camera which takes very clear photos. The man who sold it was very kind.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the following affirmative sentence into a negative sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: I have visited London three times.
targetAnswers: I haven't visited London three times.
I have not visited London three times.
practicumQuestions.explanation: To make the Present Perfect negative, add 'not' after 'have', resulting in 'haven't' or 'have not'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the following Past Simple sentence into the Present Perfect by removing the specific time phrase:
practicumQuestions.promptText: She travelled to Spain last year.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Present Perfect uses 'has' plus the past participle and does not include specific past time markers like 'last year'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Choose the correct conjunction to complete the sentence: 'We missed our train ___ we arrived late at the station.'
practicumQuestions.promptText: We missed our train ___ we arrived late at the station.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use the word that gives the reason.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use 'because' to introduce the reason why something happened.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with correct capitalization and punctuation:
practicumQuestions.promptText: my brother flew to paris on friday.
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the first word, cities, and days of the week.
targetAnswers: My brother flew to Paris on Friday.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Always capitalize the beginning of a sentence, proper city names like Paris, and days of the week like Friday.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two sentences using the relative pronoun 'who':
practicumQuestions.promptText: This is the pilot. He flew our plane to Rome.
targetAnswers: This is the pilot who flew our plane to Rome.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use 'who' to connect a person in the main clause to the relative clause describing them.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two sentences using the relative pronoun 'where':
practicumQuestions.promptText: That is the station. We caught the train there.
targetAnswers: That is the station where we caught the train.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use 'where' to refer to a place in a relative clause.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a short negative answer to the question:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Have you ever ridden a camel?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Short answers in the Present Perfect use 'Yes, I have' or 'No, I haven't'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the affirmative sentence into an interrogative question:
practicumQuestions.hint: Put 'Have' at the beginning of the sentence.
practicumQuestions.explanation: To form a question in the Present Perfect, place 'Have' or 'Has' before the subject.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the grammar error in the sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: She has take many photos on her holiday.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change 'take' to the past participle form.
targetAnswers: She has taken many photos on her holiday.
practicumQuestions.explanation: After 'has', you must use the past participle form of the verb, which is 'taken'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct transport verb: 'We had to ___ a taxi because the bus was late.'
practicumQuestions.promptText: We had to ___ a taxi because the bus was late.
practicumQuestions.hint: Think of the verb used with taxis.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In English, we use the verb 'take' with taxis, buses, trains, and planes.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Travellers Tales and Transport

content.summary: Mastering the sounds of travel vocabulary and linking words in connected speech at the A2 level.
content.audioGuidance: Focus on clear syllable stress in compound transport words and natural intonation when asking travel questions.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.explanation: Ensure distinct pronunciation of vowels in words like tram and catch.

pillars.name: Sentence Stress
pillars.explanation: Stress nouns and verbs like traveller and accommodation while weakening auxiliary words.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: The primary stress remains on the first syllable in both words.
The primary stress stays on the first syllable.
The main stress stays on the third syllable.
Notice how the stress shifts to the fourth syllable in accommodation.

drills.targetText: I need to find a cheap accommodation near the station.
drills.phonetic: /aɪ niːd tuː faɪnd ə tʃiːp əˌkɒməˈdeɪʃən nɪə ðə ˈsteɪʃən/
drills.focus: Word stress in accommodation and linking sounds
drills.hint: Pronounce each syllable clearly and emphasize the fourth syllable in accommodation.

drills.targetText: She caught the early morning tram to the city center.
drills.phonetic: /ʃiː kɔːt ði ˈɜːli ˈmɔːnɪŋ træm tuː ðə ˈsɪti ˈsentər/
drills.focus: Past tense verb catch and noun tram
drills.hint: Link caught and the smoothly together without pausing.

drills.targetText: My uncle is a famous traveller whom everyone admires.
drills.phonetic: /maɪ ˈʌŋkəl ɪz ə ˈfeɪməs ˈtrævələr huːm ˈevriwʌn ədˈmaɪərz/
drills.focus: Relative pronoun whom and verb admire
drills.hint: Emphasize the second syllable of admires.

drills.targetText: They rode their motorbikes along the long country road.
drills.phonetic: /ðeɪ rəʊd ðeə ˈməʊtəbaɪks əˈlɒŋ ðə lɒŋ ˈkʌntri rəʊd/
drills.focus: Plural nouns and compound transport words
drills.hint: Keep your voice steady on motorbikes and stress road.
